chosen.premise: Kadabra’s silver spoon isn’t decoration: without it, its psychic power is cut in half—and gold spoons apparently fail.
chosen.hook: Kadabra’s spoon has one very specific job.
chosen.visualIdea: Show a silver spoon doubling a psychic energy meter, then swap in a gold spoon as the meter drops.
chosen.note: A highly Kadabra-specific rule with a clear before-and-after visual. Multiple entries support the halved power claim, amplification, and the unusual silver-versus-gold distinction.

candidates.premise: Several Pokédex entries repeat a disturbing theory: Kadabra may have once been a psychic boy.
candidates.hook: Kadabra may not have been born a Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Follow clues from a psychic boy to a bedroom transformation, ending with a stamp reading “unverified.”
candidates.note: The transformation rumor is distinctive and highly compelling visually. However, every source frames it as a theory or rumor, so the episode must preserve that uncertainty rather than present it as fact.

candidates.premise: When Kadabra closes its eyes, twice as many alpha particles come out of its body.
candidates.hook: Kadabra gets more dangerous by closing its eyes.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen Kadabra with eyes open and closed, with twice as many glowing particles on the closed-eye side.
candidates.note: An excellent concrete contradiction—closing its eyes increases emitted alpha particles—but it is supported by only one entry and the particle effect may be hard to distinguish visually.

candidates.premise: Kadabra levitates even while asleep, using its springy tail as a pillow.
candidates.hook: Kadabra’s psychic powers work even when it’s asleep.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Kadabra drifting off the ground, then curl its springy tail beneath its head like a pillow.
candidates.note: A clean, well-supported visual gag, but the core idea is less shocking than Kadabra’s more extreme lore and does not offer much depth beyond one entry.

candidates.premise: Kadabra’s presence can reverse clocks, corrupt screens with bad-luck shadows, and ruin precision machines.
candidates.hook: Being near Kadabra can break reality’s appliances.
candidates.visualIdea: A clock reverses, a monitor fills with a creepy shadow, and precision equipment glitches as Kadabra approaches.
candidates.note: The clock, television, and machine glitches create strong visuals, but the premise combines several different effects and overstates them as “breaking reality.” Some effects occur merely through proximity, while others require psychic power.

candidates.premise: Kadabra’s psychic power increases as the danger around it gets worse.
candidates.hook: For Kadabra, danger is basically a power-up.
candidates.visualIdea: Escalate danger symbols around Kadabra while its psychic aura visibly grows stronger.
candidates.note: The danger-to-power relationship is supported, but “danger makes it stronger” is a familiar Pokémon-style power-up premise and lacks a precise scale or memorable rule.

rounds.request: The selected angle is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need one precise, unmistakably Kadabra-specific rule with equally direct source support, such as a quantified effect or a documented contradiction, while remaining easy to demonstrate visually.
